source.section: PDF page 23, Table E (MFJ/QSS, more than 100,000 to 100,500: .01); PDF page 21, Table C (MFJ 0 up to 100,500); PDF pages 19-23, Tax Calculation Schedule Lines 1-10 with Table A, Table B, Tables C-D and Table E; Form CT-1040 Lines 1-6

worked: Federal AGI = wages 100,400.00 = 100,400.00. Federal taxable income = 100,400.00 - 31,500.00 standard deduction = 68,900.00 (given, not tested; federal senior deduction ignored). CT-1040 Line 1 federal AGI 100,400.00; Line 2 additions 0.00 (Schedule 1 Lines 31-37: none apply); Line 3 = 100,400.00. Schedule 1 Line 50 total subtractions = 0.00; CT-1040 Line 4 = 0.00. CT-1040 Line 5 Connecticut AGI = 100,400.00 - 0.00 = 100,400.00. Tax Calculation Schedule Line 1 = 100,400.00; Line 2 Table A: Connecticut AGI 100,400.00 is more than 71,000.00, exemption 0.00; Line 3 taxable income = 100,400.00 - 0.00 = 100,400.00. Line 4 Table B (Married Filing Jointly/Qualifying Surviving Spouse schedule) on 100,400.00: 20,000.00 x 0.02 + 80,000.00 x 0.045 + 400.00 x 0.055 = 400.00 + 3,600.00 + 22.00 = 4,022.00. Line 5 Table C 0.00 (Connecticut AGI 100,400.00 is not more than 100,500.00); Line 6 Table D 0.00 (not more than 210,000.00); Line 7 = 4,022.00. Line 8 Table E decimal 0.01 (Connecticut AGI 100,400.00 is in the band more than 100,000.00); Line 9 = 4,022.00 x 0.01 = 40.22. Line 10 Connecticut income tax = 4,022.00 - 40.22 = 3,981.78 (CT-1040 Line 6). No other credits (property tax credit not claimed: no property tax in the inputs, and not modelled). Note: Connecticut AGI 100,400 is in the last Table E band with a credit (.01) and still not over 100,500, where Table C starts.
